subject: Data Structures
title: Discover Queues
description: Discover how a Queue stores and removes data.

mission.title: Discover FIFO
mission.description: Find the hidden rule behind a Queue.

discovery.title: First In First Out
discovery.summary: The first item added to a Queue is the first item removed.

sections.title: What is a Queue?
sections.content: A Queue is a linear data structure that keeps items in the order they arrive.

sections.title: FIFO
sections.content: FIFO means First In, First Out: the first item added is the first one removed.

sections.title: Operations
sections.content: ENQUEUE adds an item at the back. DEQUEUE removes an item from the front.

sections.title: Real-world example
sections.content: People waiting in a line are served in the same order that they joined the line.

alternate_explanations.title: Think of a waiting line
alternate_explanations.content: A Queue is like people waiting for a bus. New people join at the back, and the person at the front boards first.

alternate_explanations.title: Walk through the line
alternate_explanations.content: ENQUEUE A, then B, then C. The line is A → B → C. DEQUEUE removes A first because A has waited the longest.

introduction.title: Meet the Queue
introduction.content: A Queue keeps items in the order they arrive. You will experiment with adding items and letting them leave.
points: New items join at the REAR.
You are about to use ENQUEUE and DEQUEUE.

worked_example.title: Watch ENQUEUE and DEQUEUE
worked_example.content: Follow the Queue as each operation changes who is waiting at the front.

steps.explanation: 10 is the first item, so it is waiting at the front.
30 joins at the rear, after the other waiting items.
10 leaves from the front of the Queue.

worked_example.conclusion: 10 left because it entered the Queue first and had been waiting the longest.

next.title: Use the playground below.
next.content: Try ENQUEUE to add items at the rear, then DEQUEUE to remove the item at the front.

enqueue: 10 joined the Queue at the REAR.
20 joined behind 10. New items enter from the REAR.
30 joined behind 20. It is now at the REAR.
action_explanations.dequeue: {removed} left from the FRONT. It had been waiting the longest.

phases.feedback: Look at the target Queue and compare it with yours.

recall.title: Recall
recall.prompt: In your own words, why does a Queue remove the oldest item first?
recall.empty_message: Write a short explanation before submitting.
recall.model_answer: A Queue removes from the front. New items join at the rear, so the item that has waited the longest reaches the front and leaves first.

guidance.start_message: Build the target Queue. Watch which end is FRONT and which is REAR.

items.content: New items always join at the REAR.

phases.title: Build the waiting line
phases.feedback: Compare your Queue with the target from FRONT to REAR.

guidance.start_message: Transform the Queue without a button-by-button recipe.

items.content: Only DEQUEUE changes the FRONT; ENQUEUE always changes the REAR.

phases.title: Transform the Queue
phases.feedback: Think about which item has been waiting longest before adding anything.

solve.instruction: Transform START into TARGET with no hints. Plan from FRONT to REAR.

solve.feedback: Compare the current Queue with the target from the front.
